notes.37: Question 37 was usually well done. Examiners were looking for de plus en plus de gens qui n’ont pas assez à manger . Those who chose to state that he was shocked were expected to include a verb (e.g. il est ) as choqué et révolté on its own was not clear. For Question 38 , candidates had to provide 2 details. Most candidates were able to provide (i) cinq mille bénévoles viennent se joindre à l’Association and (ii) distribuent huit millions de repas . Even though the vast majority of candidates located the correct information for Question 39 , many lost the mark as the addition of est telle after la popularité de Coluche showed that they had not really understood. Question 40 was straightforward and the vast majority of candidates were able to offer the correct answer: Des amis de Coluche décident de continuer son travail.
notes.41: Question 41 was also well answered and most candidates scored the mark for stating ils aident ceux qui n’ont plus rien à entrer de nouveau dans la société en trouvant un emploi. FRENCH (Foreign Language)
notes.key_messages: ● To maximise their chances of success, candidates need to have a thorough knowledge of question words, beyond qui and pourquoi . Candidates need to make sure they read questions carefully and identify whether the question is asking qui or qu’est-ce que , où or quand , comment or pourquoi . ● Answers should be brief and focused, particularly in Section 3 . ● In order to do themselves justice in Section 3 , candidates need to be familiar with personal pronouns (subject and object) and possessive adjectives in the third person singular and plural. ● If an answer or part of an answer has been crossed out, it must be made as clear as possible what the Examiner is to mark. ● When candidates finish the paper, they should read it through again and check that they have answered every question and made any corrections needed.
notes.general_comments: In general, candidates had been well prepared for the paper: they seemed aware of how to approach the various exercises and appeared to have no problems completing them in the time allowed. Where questions require written answers in French, once they have read the text carefully, candidates need to look closely at what each question is asking them, and also at how much space has been allowed for their answer. Usually a single line will be provided for their answer, indicating that the answer can be given briefly, without the need to copy 3 or 4 lines of text. It is better to think a little rather than writing the first answer that comes to mind, and then perhaps having to cross it out – it can be difficult for Examiners to award marks where it is not clear what the candidate’s final answer is intended to be. It is good practice for candidates to read through their work once again after they have finished the examination. This is the moment to check that all the questions have been answered, and make any corrections, particularly to answers to the writing exercises, for example: ● subject and verb agreements; ● possessive adjectives, particularly in Section 3 , and adjective agreements in general; ● words mis-copied from the texts or instructions.
